title: Is Claude Max 5x worth it for building 3D game maps in Godot?
author: mxplr
selftext:
Hey guys!

I've been trying to create a 3D map for my FPS game in Godot, but despite experimenting with different approaches, I haven't been really happy with the overall design.

So I decided to try a different workflow: generating reference images with ChatGPT, then using Claude Code with the Gauntlet Loop to recreate those designs directly in Godot.

My goal is to have Claude generate the entire 3D map, including the scenes and environments, based on those reference images.

I'm running the Gauntlet Loop without setting a specific iteration limit. Basically, I just tell Claude to keep working until the map looks as close as possible to the reference images.

The problem is that I've already used 50% of my weekly Claude Pro allowance in just two days.

I'm considering upgrading to the Max 5x plan, but I'm wondering whether it would actually be enough for this kind of workflow, and whether it's worth the extra cost.

My main concern is that I'm spending a lot of tokens going back and forth with Claude to fix things or improve the design, and I'm not sure if upgrading my plan is the solution or if I should rethink my workflow entirely.

I'm also wondering if this is even the right approach to building complete 3D environments with AI, or if there's a more efficient way to do it.

Has anyone tried something similar? How do you handle large-scale 3D scene generation with Claude Code? Do you let it work autonomously, or do you break things down into smaller tasks?

I'd love to hear about your experiences and workflows!

comments.author: weverz
comments.body: To me the 5x plan is Just insane value when building anything 3D. If it is suitable for your work? Idk.

replies.author: mxplr
replies.body: I decided to give it a try

comments.author: aimhelix
comments.body: Yes. I started hitting week caps in 3 days. Now I have lots of headroom. But honestly still learning Claude too but right now I feel like a boss with really capable employees.
